Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this game and two arch-rivals, India and Pakistan have secured their places in the semifinals with a couple of spots still to be filled. On Wednesday, the 4th of October we will witness the remaining two quarterfinals and in the first game, Afghanistan will take on Sri Lanka at 6.30 am IST (1 am GMT). This will be followed by a match-up between Bangladesh and Malaysia starting at 11.30 am IST (6 am GMT). Both matches will be played at the same venue and you can join us in advance for the build-up as well. Cheers!

Hong Kong will be slightly disheartened with that batting display, particularly the way the middle order just crumbled against the Pakistani spinners. They did play well in patches and bowled extremely well but lost the plot and the very final over of the first innings from Ayush Shukla might have picked have a couple of wickets but he conceded 26 runs as well which handed the mental advantage to the opposition going into the break. With the bat, skipper Nizakat Khan made a decent start but lost his opening partner for a duck. It was then Babar Hayat who escaped a stumping chance and mustered up a few runs. But once they lost 4 wickets, it went downhill all too quickly for them and even a couple of little cameos at the death couldn't take them over the 100-run mark.

A very commanding victory then for Pakistan and they have taken a big step forward to get into medal contention as they zoom through into the semifinals. After a fairly difficult start with the bat, the middle order managed to get them back into the contest and the stunning cameo from Aamer Jamal allowed them to get over the 150-run mark. With the ball, however, they made a good start as Arafat Minhas got an early wicket. It was quiet for a while but once they got into that middle order, the likes of Khushdil Shah and Sufiyan Muqeem just ripped through. Slowly but surely enough Pakistan got the job done as skipper Qasim Akram himself came on and picked up the final two wickets.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length in the channel, Babar Hayat looks to play at it but is beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshad Iqbal to Babar Hayat, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and outside off, Nizakat Khan taps it wide of the man at third man and picks up a single.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Edged but safe! Flighted one, on a shorter length and outside off, Babar Hayat has a poke at it but gets an outside edge that goes sharply to the left of first slip and runs away to the fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Arafat Minhas to Babar Hayat, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Babar Hayat walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! Muhammad Khan does get bat on this one but ends up giving his wicket away. Tossed up on a length around middle and turning away. Khan looks for the slog-sweep but gets a top edge that goes just behind the keeper. Rohail Nazir has time to move back and pouch it safely. Arafat Minhas gets the first breakthrough for Pakistan.
Commentary.Howout: c Rohail Nazir b Arafat Minhas
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Arafat Minhas to Muhammad Khan, OUT! c Rohail Nazir b Arafat Minhas.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up around off, another swing and a miss by Muhammad Khan.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Arafat Minhas to Muhammad Khan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Muhammad Khan is finding it difficult to get bat on ball here. Flighted one outside off and turning away, Khan sits down to slog-sweep but misses it completely.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Arafat Minhas to Muhammad Khan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just short! Tossed up around off, Nizakat Khan looks to step out and go big but gets a thick outside edge that lands in front of short third. They pick up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Arafat Minhas to Nizakat Khan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and well wide outside off, Nizakat Khan stays back and hits it hard but straight to the man at covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Arafat Minhas to Nizakat Khan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end?
A jaffa to end the first over! Nagging length outside off and this time the ball just holds its line. Muhammad Khan looks to block but the ball just goes past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arshad Iqbal to Muhammad Khan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish length, angled at the body, Muhammad Khan looks to step out and take it on but gets nowhere near the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arshad Iqbal to Muhammad Khan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! A touch fuller on off and this one shapes away late. Muhammad Khan looks to play at it but is beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arshad Iqbal to Muhammad Khan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, Khan pushes it out toward mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arshad Iqbal to Nizakat Khan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Fuller in length but well wide of the off stump, Nizakat Khan goes after it and slashes it away wide of the fielder at third man for a one-bounce boundary. Hong Kong are up and running here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arshad Iqbal to Nizakat Khan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! What a way to get the run chase underway! Full on middle to start with, minimal foot movement from Nizakat Khan but he uses those wrists well and whips it away in front of square on the leg side to get off the mark with a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arshad Iqbal to Nizakat Khan, Four!
